title: 10-Hydroxy-2-decenoic acid ameliorates LPS-induced acute lung injury through targeting MD2-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways.
authors: Shu, Cong; Li, Chen; Liu, Huamin; Zhou, Zengxian; Qian, Chenghao; Xie, Zhuohui; Lin, Fenfen; Jiang, Yuxiao; Chen, Ruping; Liu, Yue; Liu, Xin; Chen, Gaozhi; Fu, Lili
one_liner_zh: 该文研究10-HDA通过分子对接靶向MD2抑制LPS诱导的急性肺损伤炎症通路，虽涉及蛋白-小分子对接，但核心是药物抗炎机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute lung injury (ALI) and its severe form, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), are life-threatening conditions with high mortality, characterized by excessive inflammatory responses. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is widely used to mimic ALI by activating myeloid differentiation factor 2 (MD2)/Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated inflammatory pathways. Royal jelly-derived 10-hydroxy-2-decenoic acid (10-HDA) exhibits anti-inflammatory properties, but its role in ALI remains unexplored. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of 10-HDA against LPS-induced ALI and elucidate its underlying mechanism. METHODS: In vitro, mouse peritoneal macrophages (MPMs) were pretreated with 10-HDA before LPS stimulation. In vivo, ALI was induced in mice via intratracheal LPS, with 10-HDA administered intraperitoneally. Cytokine levels were measured via ELISA and qPCR. Signaling pathways were analyzed by Western blot and immunofluorescence. Lung injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and edema were assessed via histopathology, BALF analysis, and wet/dry ratio. Immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, and drug affinity-responsive target stability (DARTS) assays were used to identify the interaction between 10-HDA and MD2. RESULTS: 10-HDA significantly suppressed LPS-induced proinflammatory cytokine secretion in MPMs and ALI mice, and inhibited phosphorylation of TAK1, MAPKs, TBK1 and NF-kappaB nuclear translocation. It attenuated lung histopathological damage, neutrophil infiltration, and edema. Mechanistically, 10-HDA disrupted MD2/TLR4-mediated inflammatory pathways by directly binding MD2, as confirmed by immunoprecipitation, DARTS, and molecular docking. CONCLUSION: 10-HDA alleviates LPS-induced ALI by targeting MD2 to block TLR4 signaling, thereby suppressing both MyD88-dependent (MAPKs/NF-kappaB) and TRIF-dependent (TBK1/IRF3) pathways. These findings highlight 10-HDA as a promising therapeutic candidate for ALI/ARDS.
abstract_zh: 背景：急性肺损伤（ALI）及其严重形式急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ARDS）是危及生命且死亡率高的疾病，其特征为过度炎症反应。脂多糖（LPS）通过激活髓样分化因子2（MD2）/Toll样受体4（TLR4）介导的炎症通路，被广泛用于模拟ALI。蜂王浆来源的10-羟基-2-癸烯酸（10-HDA）具有抗炎特性，但其在ALI中的作用尚未被探索。目的：本研究旨在探讨10-HDA对LPS诱导的ALI的治疗潜力，并阐明其潜在机制。方法：体外实验中，小鼠腹膜巨噬细胞（MPMs）在LPS刺激前用10-HDA预处理。体内实验中，通过气管内注射LPS诱导小鼠ALI，并腹腔注射10-HDA。通过ELISA和qPCR测量细胞因子水平。通过Western blot和免疫荧光分析信号通路。通过组织病理学、BALF分析和湿/干比评估肺损伤、炎症细胞浸润和水肿。使用免疫沉淀、分子对接和药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）实验来鉴定10-HDA与MD2之间的相互作用。结果：10-HDA显著抑制了LPS诱导的MPMs和ALI小鼠中促炎细胞因子的分泌，并抑制了TAK1、MAPKs、TBK1的磷酸化及NF-kappaB核转位。它减轻了肺组织病理损伤、中性粒细胞浸润和水肿。机制上，10-HDA通过直接结合MD2破坏MD2/TLR4介导的炎症通路，这一点通过免疫沉淀、DARTS和分子对接得到证实。结论：10-HDA通过靶向MD2阻断TLR4信号，从而抑制MyD88依赖性（MAPKs/NF-kappaB）和TRIF依赖性（TBK1/IRF3）通路，缓解LPS诱导的ALI。这些发现凸显了10-HDA作为ALI/ARDS有前景的治疗候选药物。
